terms.gloss: a law; in the plural, the laws
evidence: Traupman 195: against the law, contrā lēgem; by law, lēge
terms.comment: A particular law, passed by the people: lēgem ferre, to propose a law (Traupman 180); contrā lēgem, against a law; lēge, by law (Traupman 195).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.33: summum jūs summa injūria
terms.comment: The law as a body, and what is right by it: contrā jūs, against the law (Traupman 195); jūs cīvīle, the civil law, as a subject of study.

phrases.latin: plūsque ibi bonī mōrēs valent quam alibī bonae lēgēs
phrases.english: and good customs count for more there than good laws elsewhere

phrases.latin: ollīs salūs populī suprēma lēx estō
phrases.english: for them the safety of the people shall be the highest law

phrases.latin: ex quō illud ‘summum jūs summa injūria’ factum est jam trītum sermōne prōverbium
phrases.english: hence “the strictest law is the greatest injustice” has become a common proverb
to ratify a bill (of the people voting it into law)
against the law (against a particular law)

phrases.source: Traupman 195; cf. Suet. Caes. 43: lēgem sūmptuāriam (Lewis & Short s.v. exerceō)

phrases.english: to throw the book at someone (literally “to deal with him by the full rigour of the law”)
phrases.source: Traupman 197; cf. Cic. Off. 1.33: summō jūre agere (Lewis & Short s.v. agō)

phrases.latin: Spērō jūdicem summō jūre cum istīs āctūrum esse.
phrases.english: I hope the judge throws the book at them.
